works.author: Oecumenius of Tricca
works.authorNote: 10th-century Byzantine bishop/compiler; PG 118-119 gathers the Greek catena tradition on Paul's Epistles (and, per the parent volume's own preface, possibly the Acts/Catholic-epistle catena too) under his name — attribution to a single 'Oecumenius' is itself debated in scholarship, but PG's ascription is what this citation follows.
works.title: Commentarius in Epistolam ad Philippenses
works.titleEn: Commentary on the Epistle to the Philippians
works.queueNote: PG paired-pilot P3 (pg-paired-pilot.md §7): the spec recommended the commentary on Jude (or 2-3 John) as the volume's smallest complete lemma-and-gloss unit, on the assumption Catholic-epistle commentary is in PG 118. It is NOT: the local Calfa harvest of PG118_text.txt (37,508 lines) runs Romans through Philippians only (ends mid-volume with the doxology 'Τέλος σὺν Θεῷ τῆς πρὸς Φιλιππησίους'); Jude/2-3 John and the rest of the Pauline corpus (Colossians onward) are apparently in PG 119 or simply outside this Calfa clone's scope — not investigated further, per rule 8 (don't hunt past what's in hand). Philippians (14,089 Greek words, Calfa pp. 641-674) is the smallest complete epistle-commentary actually present in the file, smaller than Galatians (15,862w) and Ephesians (18,927w), the file's other short candidates. It is lemma-and-gloss throughout (scriptural lemma in quotation marks, then gloss — e.g. opens '«Τοῖς ἁγίοις ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.» Ἦσαν γὰρ καὶ Ἰουδαῖοι...'), satisfying the genre purpose of P3 even though the specific book differs from the recommendation. NOTE: translationStatus deliberately absent (no verified none-status is in hand for this specific work; the deploy badge fails safe to 'New English translation' per CLAUDE.md rule 8 — do not hunt to fill this in).

Latin twin is UNAVAILABLE for those 3 pages; the Latin twin chunks that span them are correspondingly under-length (see src/pg-latin/isidore-glabas-sermo-1/manifest.json). GAP CLOSED 2026-07-31 (coordinator follow-up): patrologicursus73migngoog.pdf (702pp, a second archive.org item / different physical-copy scan) DOES carry all three missing columns intact at PDF pages 10 (cols 11-12), 11 (cols 13-14), and 18 (cols 27-28) -- confirmed by direct page inspection plus tesseract grc+lat OCR, >=2 distinctive Greek tokens per page (4, 4, 3 hits). works.queueNote: Sermon III of Isidore Glabas's Sermones IV in B. Mariam Virginem (parent `isidore-glabas-sermones`, PG 139, 11-164) -- the Annunciation sermon, third of the four, queued per pg-paired-pilot.md 8a.C after Sermons I and II shipped. Span from the Calfa headings: LOGOS G' opens 55 chars into page 43 (the same page/column where Sermon II ends) and Sermon IV opens 309 chars into page 66, so both ends are truncated by data/calfa-patches/isidore-glabas-sermo-3.json. WARNING recorded at queueing: Calfa OCRs Sermon IV's heading as 'KOIOS D'' rather than 'LOGOS D'', so a grep for the correct heading reports Sermon IV absent and would have run this work past its own ending to the end of the volume. The boundary was found by reading, not by grepping the heading. translationStatus inherited from the parent entry's 2026-07-03 verification, which covered all four sermons; it has NOT been re-verified per-sermon, so this work must not carry a 'First' claim without its own check. ⚠ LATIN SEAM BLEED, measured at harvest: the Latin twin is cropped page-atomically and knows nothing of the sermon seams that the Greek-side calfa patches enforce, so the twin carries a NEIGHBOURING sermon's Latin at both ends -- 263 chars of Sermon II's close at the head of chunk 0 (up to 'per infinita saecula saeculorum. Amen.', after which 'SERMO III. In Annuntiationem...' opens) and 1,539 chars of Sermon IV at the tail of chunk 6 (from 'SERMO IV. - In summe venerandam dormitionem...', char 6,625 of 8,164). The twin is a VERIFIER, never a source, so this is safe as long as that rule holds -- Sermon II shipped under the identical condition and its English absorbed none of it, checked 2026-08-05. But a translator who reaches for the Latin will find Latin with no Greek counterpart at both seams and must not restore it. Name this in the translation prompt for every sermon split out of a parent work.
works.titleNote: Latin title is Migne's own, read off the parallel column at 0071 (the scan OCRs it 'Annnntiationem gloriosg ... Dominz ... Deiparg'; the obvious OCR artefacts are normalised, nothing else). Measured: the EPISTOLAE title block sits on leaf970 (cols 1837/1838) and the Greek of Ep. Α΄ begins in the LEFT column = col 1837, in that column's D band only — col 1837 is LATIN above the rule (the tail of Doctrina XXIV) and GREEK below it. The epistles close at '…εὐχαῖς πάντων τῶν ἁγίων. Ἀμήν.' partway down leaf972 (col 1841); a printed rule follows, then INDEX CAPITUM, which runs to the end of leaf973 (col 1844). So 1843–1844 are index, not epistle text. ⚠ Doctrina XXIV is LATIN-ONLY — Migne's own index lists 23 Greek entries against 24 Latin.
